Starting Capacity

In The Expanse RPG, characters begin with a default Capacity of 0. Characters must improve their Capacity in order to avoid exceeding their implant Capacity.

Improving Capacity

Characters can improve their Capacity when leveling (see Advancement in Chapter 2) by trading a leveling improvement for +1 Capacity. No more than one Capacity improvement can be taken per level earned, unless the Game Master decides otherwise.

Exceeding Capacity

Capacity is the amount a character’s body can be modified safely. However, players may choose to add implant enhancements beyond their capacity if the GM allows it. Cheaper or poor-quality implants have also been known to have similar effects as exceeding Capacity. No specific rules for this are included, but GMs should feel free to make this an option for characters seeking affordable implants. Characters may be able to mix-and-match different effects from exceeding their Capacity. In any case, the GM should set a reasonable limit on exceeding Capacity, usually a maximum of 6 slots, if this option is allowed at all in the game. The considerable strain on the character’s body or mind imposes one of the following effects:

ABILITY REDUCTION One of the character’s ability scores is reduced by 1 per slot the character is over Capacity. So, the character might suffer a penalty to Strength, Intelligence, Willpower―any ability, so long as it is approved by the GM. The ability affected reflects the type of strain the character is under: Strength is muscle weakness or degradation, Intelligence is loss of cognitive function, and so forth.

SIDE EFFECTS The character suffers a side effect after the augment is activated or at the end of the scene. They immediately lose 1d6 + (slots over Capacity) Fortune. Alternately, the GM (or the player with the GMs permission) can come up with other possible side effects. They can recover this lost Fortune normally, likely spending time and resources doing so. This effect only applies to implants that are activated. Implants with persistent effects cannot have this effect. Clarrisa Mao’s black market augmentations are a good example of how side effects could affect a player character.

THE CHURN Exceeding the character’s capacity causes other problems. The GM can increase the Churn Pool equal to the number of slots over Capacity to impose stunt effects on the character during each adventure. So, for a character who is 2 slots over Capacity, the GM could increase the Churn by 2. This Churn level renews at the start of every adventure so long as the character remains over Capacity. See The Churn in Chapter 12: Game Mastering for more details on augment-related Churn effects.

Expanse characters can acquire enhancement implants in two phases: during character creation and/or after the campaign has begun. A character who has one or more enhancement implants is an enhanced human, although different—and more colorful—names are also used, such as cyber, wired, ‘borg, hacked, juiced, or augmented, to name a few.

Character Creation Enhancement Implants

Players can fill any Capacity slots available to their characters with augmentations the Game Master says are available in the setting. It is up to the player to develop a suitable backstory for how the character got their enhancement implants based on the character’s social class, background, profession—and the nature of the setting. Encourage players to be creative in terms of detailing the backstory of their characters’ enhancements. Possibilities may include:

  • A soldier who was enhanced for service and allowed to keep the implants upon mustering out—or after deserting and disappearing into the underworld.
  • A criminal enhanced by an OPA faction or crime syndicate who may still hold a debt the character owes.
  • An upper-class character who paid for their own enhancement implants or had them paid for by family or other wealthy allies.
  • A mega-corporate (Protogen or Pope Industries) employee who received their enhancement implants as a condition or benefit of their employment, past or present.
  • A character (likely low-class or incarcerated) enhanced against their will as an experiment or some form of human trafficking.
  • A Belter who saved up to get gravity adaptation enhancements to be able to better operate on the worlds beyond the Ring.

Acquiring Enhancement Implants In-Play

After character creation, acquiring new enhancement implants requires two things: available Capacity and access to the desired implants. The player provides the available Capacity by improving it while leveling (see Improving Capacity, previously), having some previously unused Capacity, or by removing an existing implant to free up space. The Game Master generally provides access as part of a reward. This may be a favor or other payment owed to the character, the benefit of a level of Membership, or access granted by a Relationship, to name a few. In essence, it is up to the GM when to greenlight the ability to fill additional Capacity and what enhancement implants are available when the characters can do so. Realistically, adding enhancements takes a considerable amount of money to pay for the medical procedures, recovery, and the implant itself. This is even more expensive when the work is done illegally or on the black market. Rather than go through complex formulae to figure out the huge costs of augmentation work, it makes more sense from a campaign perspective to have the Game Master control and provide access. If a player really wants a particular augmentation, but their character hasn’t managed to earn enough to obtain it, the Game Master can always provide riskier opportunities for the character, like working with a loan shark or agreeing to take on dangerous (and higher-playing) work for clients who can provide the money or access.

pages.name: Enhancement Implants: Biological and Synthetic Enhancement Implants

text.content: Unless an enhancement specifically involves technological parts or capabilities, such as a built-in radio or computer, the implant may be either biological or synthetic in nature. Visual implants, for example, may involve cloned or surgically altered biological eyes or cybernetic replacements. Some biological enhancements may be the result of genetic engineering, either in utero encoded into the character’s DNA (for enhancement implants selected during character creation) or grown in the character through gene-editing, leading to a new phenotype (the expression of a creature’s genetic traits within an environment).

As opposed to enhancements, which improve a character’s abilities, alterations are primarily or entirely “cosmetic” in that they may change the character’s appearance in various ways and may be personally important to the character and their quality of life, but they do not provide any game-related effects or abilities. Cosmetic alterations have no impact on a character’s Capacity and merely cost the necessary Resources and access to acquire them. Examples of cosmetic alterations in an Expanse setting may include:

BODY ALTERATION Any change to the character’s body that doesn’t affect their game traits. This can be as minor as a permanent change of eye- or hair-color to changing sexual characteristics (making the character a different sex or intersex) or providing scales, skin colors not found in nature (like blue, green, or purple, for example), fiber-optic “hair,” and prosthetic replacement of body parts, including limbs, and other assistive or corrective technology. The only limits to body alteration are the players’ imaginations, the setting’s available technology, and the requirement they have no in-game benefits.

BODY ART These are effectively permanent additions to the character’s appearance, from low-tech tattoos and scarification to more much involved body art, possibly involving light- or heat-activated or even moving inks, and other surgical alterations in appearance. Piercings can fall into this category, although they’re only semi-permanent (depending on their placement and long-term usage) and relatively inexpensive compared to some body art.

Enhancement implants can provide several different game system benefits. The following section outlines the major benefits, how they work, and their relative value in terms of how easy or difficult they are to acquire. The latter is described in numerical “enhancements” (one implant, two implants, and so on). Note that these benefits are the “bare bones” of enhancement implant design: The GM should exercise some oversight when it comes to defining enhancements in the game and should feel free to modify the results of these guidelines to best suit the game’s style and setting. The Enhancement Implant Catalog section provides several examples of how you can tweak or modify the basic effects and mechanics to come up with any number of unique enhancements for your game.

ABILITY

This effect is essentially equivalent to an ability advancement; for abilities with scores of 5 or less, this amounts to a +1 increase to that ability. For higher ability scores, additional enhancements are needed to increase the ability: Abilities from 6 to 8 require two, and abilities from 9 to 13 require three. There’s no real functional difference between an ability enhancement and an ability advancement except the enhancement is artificial and effectively occurs all at once whereas ability advancement reflects practice, training, and experience. Still, it may be a useful effect for certain implants. At the Game Master’s discretion, enhancement implants can ignore the normal rules for ability advancement, which say the same ability cannot be advanced two levels (or two advancements) in a row. For enhancement implants, the sole limit is the character’s available slots and Capacity, so someone with 3 available slots could go from a score of 2 in an ability to a score of 5 all at once. It is also up to the Game Master which abilities can be enhanced using implants.

ABILITY FOCUS

An effect can grant the benefits of an ability focus, particularly for a somatic ability, or the equivalent of an ability focus—a +2 bonus with tests—for a similarly narrow use of an ability. For example, this could be a bonus on tests to avoid a particular hazard or to perform a particular task not already covered by an existing focus. In instances where an ability focus enhancement would stack with an existing focus, the combined bonus is considered +3 (rather than +4).

ACTION

The action effect changes your options for actions on your turn in action time (see Taking Actions in Chapter 5).

FAST ACTION One enhancement lets you take a specific major action as a minor action on your turn. You could, for example, use a type of attack or defend as a minor action. Choose the action when you take the enhancement.

EXTRA ACTION One enhancement allows you to take an additional minor action on your turn.

REACTION One enhancement allows you to choose a specific major or minor action and always have it prepared, able to use it with a minor action at any time in reaction to a particular circumstance, even when it is not your turn in the initiative order. You define the action and circumstance when you choose this enhancement.

SECOND CHANCE One enhancement allows you to choose a particular ability focus. If you fail an ability test involving that focus, you can re-roll the test and use the result of the second roll.

Characters are limited to a maximum of one major and two minor actions on their turn, even with this enhancement, although they may be able to also perform certain major actions as minor actions.

DEFENSE

This effect grants you either +1 to your Defense or +1 to your Toughness. The GM should set reasonable limits on the additional Defense or Toughness characters can gain, such as a bonus no more than one-third of their level, rounded up.

FAVORED STUNT

Choose a specific stunt available for use in the setting. Each enhancement applied to this effect reduces the stunt’s SP cost for you by 1. If you reduce the stunt’s SP cost to 0, you can perform that stunt at-will whenever there is an opportunity to do so. So, for example, if you have Favored Stunt (Disarm) with two enhancements, any time you hit an armed opponent with a melee attack, you can attempt to disarm them, whether you have rolled stunt points or not.

Additionally, you can perform the Activate action for your Favored Stunt, gaining 2 Stunt Point when you do so, much like a use of Stunt Attack. You must perform your Favored Stunt with your next major action.

FORCE MULTIPLIER

Choose a particular task largely defined by an ability focus, such as Strength (Jumping) or Intelligence (Research). With one enhancement, you are twice as effective at that task when you succeed in performing it. With two enhancements, you are five times as effective. Examples include:

JUMPING Your Force Multiplier affects the distance you can jump with a successful test.

LIFTING Your Force Multiplier increases the amount you can lift, beginning with twice that of someone of your Strength.

RESEARCH Divide the time the research takes by your Force Multiplier.

RUNNING When you take the Run action, your Force Multiplier increases your Speed. It does not affect your Speed for ordinary Move actions during action time, however. Whereas the Ability enhancement (previously) improves the actual ability score, and therefore benefits tests with that ability; a Force Multiplier improves what you can accomplish with the same ability within a particular defined area. Note that Expanse characters are limited to two Force Multiplier enhancements (a ×10 multiplier).

HAZARD IMMUNITY

Choose a particular type of environmental hazard. For a number of enhancements equal to the hazard’s category—one for minor, two for moderate, and so on—you are essentially immune to that hazard. See Hazards in Chapter 12 for details. Common examples include immunity to drowning (essentially, the ability to breathe underwater) or a short (10-foot) fall for one enhancement, immunity to suffocation, a longer fall immunity to environmental cold or heat, or to diseases or toxins for two enhancements. Note that an Expanse character cannot have more than two Hazard Immunity enhancements.

INNATE ATTACK

You have some sort of innate damaging attack beyond just a person’s usual unarmed abilities. With one enhancement, your innate attack does 1d6 damage in close combat. Each additional enhancement increases its damage by 1d6, to a maximum of 3d6. Choose an ability and focus you use for your attack roll with the Innate Attack, such as Fighting (Brawling) or Accuracy (Pistols). At the GM’s discretion, you may have a special focus for this attack to replace another of your ability focuses. You may also choose an ability score to add to your innate attack’s damage, either Strength, Dexterity, or Perception. These choices do not change once they are made. If you have talents that confer damage bonuses, they may apply to your Innate Attack provided it is of the appropriate type. For example, an “unarmed” damage bonus might apply to an Innate Attack involving claws or steel-hard fists. Consult the GM in cases where it is not clear whether a bonus should apply. For an additional enhancement, your innate attack can be used at range, with a range of 50 meters. A second enhancement doubles this range to 100 meters. Finally, for a separate additional enhancement, your innate attack can cause Penetrating damage, but you must halve the damage after it is rolled, rounding up.

SPECIAL STUNT

Create a special or unique stunt, one that does not exist in the rulebook. As an enhancement, your character can perform this new stunt at its normal stunt point cost. Often a special stunt implies or relies on capabilities ordinary people do not have, such as a Stunt Punch stunt, allowing you to generate a burst of electricity and inflict an additional 1d6 Penetrating electrical damage with a successful unarmed strike for 2 stunt points. The GM should approve the final SP cost and mechanics of the new stunt. Special stunts are useful for augmentations that have unpredictable or variable effects or that do not always come into play, but function more like regular stunts. You can apply the benefits of the Favored Stunt effect (previously) to a Special Stunt, reducing its SP cost. If it is reduced to 0, you can perform the Special Stunt at-will whenever there is an opportunity to do so, the same as with a regular Favored Stunt.

PERQUISITE

As an enhancement, you gain a single specific benefit or advantage (a perquisite or “perk”) that’s useful but does not otherwise conform to the benefits given previously. Perquisites can be almost anything the player and GM can agree upon, from the ability to project a beam of light equivalent to a flashlight at will to malleable facial features giving you the benefit of always having a “disguise kit” or an implanted hand terminal. A good guideline for a perquisite is the innate benefit of a minor piece of equipment or the like. The Game Master may rule that some perks require more than one enhancement, particularly if they are multi-functional or have broad benefits.

Just as the Game Master can decide whether to allow extraordinary abilities in the game at all, the GM can also set limits on the benefits available from enhancements, ranging from no more than X enhancements spent on a particular benefit (say 1–3) or no Innate Attack or Innate Power enhancements, no reducing stunt point costs below 1, or any other guidelines the GM wishes to establish. Just because an enhancement is potentially possible in the context of the game rules does not mean a player automatically has the option to acquire it for their character in a particular campaign. As always, the needs and design of The Expanse setting take precedence.

pages.name: Enhancement Implants: The Enhancement Implant Catalog

text.content:
The following is a catalog of enhancement implants that may exist in an Expanse setting, but it is up to the Game Master to decide which of these options exist and how widely available they might be. Some of these enhancement implants also mention campaign limits, which can be set by the Game Master using the guidelines from Enhancement Implant Effects (earlier in this chapter) to determine the maximum effectiveness of the implant and how many enhancements can be applied to it.

Adrenal Enhancement 2 Slots

Your enhanced adrenaline surges in times of stress. You can perform the Adrenaline Rush stunt for −1 SP cost and can perform a special Adrenaline Surge stunt that grants you a lifting and pushing force multiplier on your Strength (Might) tests: x2 for 2 SP.

Av Memory 1 Slot

You can record everything you see and hear as if you were a high-res video camera and download it to external digital storage through a concealed port. With the Commlink augmentation (following), you can also download and transmit your sensory feed wirelessly like a live video broadcast.

Blood Filters 1+ Slot

Special filters and binding agents in your bloodstream reduce the damage of any contact or injected toxin by 1 die. If this reduces the damage dice to 0, the toxin simply doesn’t affect you. You also cannot become drunk while you have this enhancement, regardless of how much alcohol you consume. More effective blood filters require additional enhancements and reduce toxin damage by 1 die per additional enhancement, up to 5. Alternately, 1 slot of this augmentation can instead give you total immunity to a single specific toxin that it targets while having no effect against others.

Chameleon Skin 1 Slot

Special chromatophores in your epidermal layer allow you to change color to blend into your surroundings. When making Dexterity (Stealth) tests, you can perform a special Blend- In stunt, adding +1 per SP spent to the target number for a

Combat Reflexes 1 Slot

Enhanced muscle memory and amped-up reflexes built for combat situations allow you to make melee attacks as a minor action rather than a major action. This means you can make two such attacks per turn using both your major and minor actions or take a different major action and still make a melee attack as a minor action. This augmentation does not benefit ranged attacks.

Commlink 1 Slot

You have an implanted computer and radio transmitter and receiver able to perform all the functions of a hand terminal or similar mobile device, including connecting to local terminal communication networks. You control the commlink by thought and visual cues and do not have to speak aloud to transmit or operate it. You can use this augmentation in conjunction with others able to receive or transmit data.

Cybernetic Arm 1 Slot

One of your arms is replaced with a cybernetic prosthesis, as effective as a real limb, but also with a x2 Force Multiplier for Strength tests and actions related solely to your arm and hand. With two enhancements, both arms are augmented. An additional enhancement increases the force multiplier of your cybernetic arm to five times as strong as normal. A cybernetic arm that simply serves as a replacement prosthesis, with no enhanced abilities, requires no Capacity and is considered a “cosmetic” effect.

Cybernetic Ear 1+ Slot

One or both of your ears are replaced or improved with implanted technology. For each enhancement applied, choose one of the following:

  • You gain the Perception (Hearing) focus, or increase its bonus by +1, if you already have it.
  • You gain a ×2 Force Multiplier for your hearing, able to hear over twice normal distances. Additional enhancements can improve this multiplier.
  • You gain the ability to hear especially high- or low-pitched sounds (choose one) beyond the normal human hearing range.
  • Your ears automatically compensate for extremely loud noises and other overstimulation. Your hearing cannot be disabled by such attacks or environmental hazards.
  • If you fail a test involving your hearing, you can re-roll and use the second result.

A cybernetic ear that simply replaces your existing ears or restores your hearing to normal human levels counts as a 0-slot cosmetic alteration. The same is also true for alterations to the shape and appearance of your ears, from pointed “elf ears” to more animalistic designs to removing your exterior ears entirely while retaining your normal hearing.

Cybernetic Eye 1+ Slot

One or both of your eyes are replaced or improved with implanted technology. For each enhancement applied, choose one of the following:

  • You gain the Perception (Seeing) focus, or increase its bonus by +1, if you already have it.
  • You can see normally in the dark, as if it were lit, out to 10 meters.
  • You can see infrared heat signatures out to 10 meters. Among other things, this means you can pick out warm-blooded creatures and machines if they are warmer than the surrounding temperature and gain a +2 bonus on tests to track such subjects within a few minutes of their passage by the residual heat.
  • You can visualize radio waves and things like wireless networks and communications systems. This allows you to see the various networking “clouds” around you and to see radio sources within your visual range, including things like active commlinks.
  • You gain a ×2 Force Multiplier for your sight, able to see over twice the normal distance. Additional enhancements can improve this multiplier. You do not incur a −2 penalty to attack rolls with ranged weapons at ×1.5 range with this augmentation.
  • Your eyes automatically compensate for bright light and other overstimulation, meaning you cannot be blinded or otherwise have your vision disabled by such attacks or environmental hazards.
  • If you fail a test involving your vision, you can re-roll and use the second result.

A cybernetic eye that replaces your existing eye or restores your vision to normal human levels counts as a 0-slot cosmetic alteration. This is also true of eye replacements that change the appearance of your eyes, including things such as cat- or goat-like pupils, exotic colors, changes to the sclera or iris (including making your eyes one solid apparent color), and so forth.

Cybernetic Larynx 1 Slot

Your voice box and vocal cords are replaced and augmented. This allows you to change your voice to mimic a wide range of sounds in addition to simply disguising it. You get a +2 bonus on Communication (Deception) tests involving vocal mimicry and to Communication (Performing) tests for singing.

Cybernetic Leg 1 Slot

One of your legs is replaced with a cybernetic prosthetic, twice as strong and effective for Strength tests related solely to your leg. With two slots, both legs are augmented. In this case, add twice your Dexterity score to determine your Speed, and you can jump twice the normal distances. A cybernetic leg that simply serves as a replacement prosthesis, with no enhanced abilities, has no Capacity cost and is considered a “cosmetic” modification. This includes legs with unusual configurations like digitigrade (letting you walk on your toes like canine or feline) or leg-blades, which serve a similar function.

Dermal Reinforcement 1 Slot

You gain +1 Toughness due to reinforcement of your dermal layer using carbon fiber, ballistic memory materials, and the like. Each additional enhancement grants another +1 Toughness. Your dermal reinforcement stacks with armor worn over it, but the alterations to your epidermis make it clear your flesh is armored, ranging from a scaly texture of tiny overlapping armor plates to a thick, leathery texture. You can choose the cosmetic effect, so long as the augmentation is evident. For another additional slot, your Dermal Reinforcement is subcutaneous and otherwise concealed, meaning it is not visible or noticeable until it stops damage.

Fast Reflexes 1 Slot

You can perform the Momentum (General Combat) stunt for −1 SP cost, meaning you automatically gain +3 to initiative (for 0 SP) and can gain +6 or +9 to initiative for a round by spending 1 or 2 SP. In some settings, this augmentation may exist in multiple levels, granting an additional −1 SP cost to

Momentum (and an additional permanent +3 to initiative) per additional slot.

Gecko Pads 1 Slot

Your hands and feet have powerful micro-adhesion pads you can deploy at will. This allows you to automatically succeed on tests to climb walls and other sheer surfaces, although the GM may require a Strength (Climbing) test for Imposing or Nigh Impossible climbs, with a +8 bonus to your roll. It takes an Activate action to deploy or stop using your gecko pads, you cannot use them through materials covering your hands and feet, and you have a +2 Difficulty to actions involving your hands and feet other than climbing while they are active.

Gravity Adaptation 1+ Slot

This enhancement is a host of minor bio and cyber adjustments that allow characters used to microgravity or low gravity to function normally in full (1 g) gravity. They do not suffer any of the usual penalties for functioning in higher gravity as described in Chapter 2 of this book. An Earther who takes this augmentation can function under heavy gravity normally. Each additional slot purchased allows the character to function at one level of gravity higher.

Gyroscopic Balance 1 Slot

Your inner ears are augmented, giving you improved balance and a +2 bonus on Dexterity (Acrobatics) tests and any tests to avoid hazards, stunts, or other effects that would throw you off-balance or cause you to become prone.

Internal Compartment 1 Slot

You have a hidden internal compartment in your torso or your limbs, large enough to contain small items weighing a total of about 1 kilogram. It requires a TN 19 Perception (Seeing) test or a full body-scan to locate this compartment when it is closed. In the latter case, it still requires a TN 13 Intelligence (Electronics) test to notice anything unusual.

Joint Flexibility 1 Slot

Your joints and tendons are augmented with highly durable, elastic materials. This allows you to squeeze or fold down considerably, such that you can fit through any space large enough to accommodate your head with a TN 11 Dexterity (Stealth) test. You can also slip out of any bindings (handcuffs, ropes, etc.) that do not automatically tighten with a major action and a TN 11 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) test.

Kill-Switch 0 Slots

Augmentations make it possible to install a “kill-switch” in a subject, from a tiny explosive at the base of the brainstem to a time- or signal-release toxin, an electrical jolt that stops the heart, or an artificial stroke from blood vessel constriction. In some cases, a kill-switch might also be able to merely render you unconscious or incapacitate you with overwhelming pain instead of killing you. Usually, a kill-switch can be activated remotely, although it might also be on a timer, or keyed to some other conditions, such as a GPS sensor for when you leave or enter a particular place, or if you are exposed to a particular trigger. These types of self-destruct implants are often used as “insurance policies” to protect investments and prevent augments from absconding with expensive hardware. Game Masters can use kill-switch implants as a complication for characters who exceed their Capacity (see Exceeding Capacity at the start of this section). In essence, the character is beholden to whomever holds the control for their Kill-Switch. This provides the story explanation for why the character has augmentations in excess of their normal Capacity, and how they are “paying” for them. The existence of a Kill Switch could also be introduced as the result of an epic Churn effect. For example, during the course of the adventure, the character discovers that they have a Kill- Switch, which creates new story possibilities.

Lightning Reflexes 1 Or 2 Slots

Your amped-up reflexes are designed for making snap

Combat) stunt for just 1 SP instead of the usual 3. For two slots dedicated to this augmentation, you can perform a Lightning Attack at will, giving you a free second attack on each turn that you take an attack action.

Mag Pads 1 Slot

Magnetic pads inserted into the feet allow a character to move about in microgravity as if they are wearing magnetic boots—as long as they have a magnetic surface on which to walk. The magnetic pads function even while wearing foot coverings as long as they are not very thick and made of a non-metallic material.

Med-Injector 1 Slot

Implanted drug and stimulant injectors allow you to take a breather once during an encounter with an Activate action (see Breathers in Chapter 5 ). The Med-Injector also activates automatically if you are reduced to 0 Fortune.

Metabolic Control 1 Slot

You can exercise conscious control over your autonomic and metabolic functions. You can slow your respiration to one-quarter normal while remaining conscious and functional, although you cannot Run or Charge. You gain a +2 bonus on tests to fool equipment scanning your vital signs, such as polygraphs. You can also put yourself into a state of metabolic suspension, temporarily halting the effects of any disease or toxin in your system and consuming virtually no air. It requires a TN 17 Intelligence (Medicine) test to determine you are not actually deceased. You can revive from this state at will or at a preset time.

Microgravity Adaptation 1 Slot

Your body has a host of minor adjustments to make you better suited to long-term life in microgravity. You do not experience bone density loss and your muscles atrophy at a much slower rate. Simple, regular exercise keeps you in healthy shape. Your inner ear and sense of balance are such that you’re not easily disorientated by a lack of gravity, and you ignore any penalties for moving and operating in free-fall. This adaptation is common for Earthers who move to the Belt—and can afford it.

Targeting System 1 Slot

You have a built-in targeting system for ranged attacks, allowing you to perform the Precision Marksmanship (Gun) stunt for −1 SP cost. If you make an attack with a firearm that benefits from an aim bonus before the end of your next turn, you automatically gain a +1 bonus, even without spending SP.

Weapon Implant 1+ Slots

You have a concealed weapon implanted in your body, vate action when you want to use it. It is a TN 19 Perception (Seeing) test to notice your weapon implant when it is retracted, barring the use of scanning technology able to penetrate your skin. The nature of the weapon and its capabilities determine how many slots the augmentation requires:

CLAWS - 1 SLOT Short, sharp blades emerge from under your fingernails, letting you inflict 1d6 + Strength Impact damage with a Fighting (Brawling) attack.

SPIKES - 1 SLOT Short, blunt spikes emerge from your knuckles, inflicting 1d6 + Strength Impact damage with a Fighting (Brawling) attack.

BLADES - 2 SLOTS Longer blades pop out of your wrist or just above your knuckles, stored in your forearms. They inflict 1d6 + 3 + Strength damage using either Fighting (Brawling) or (Light Blades), as you choose.

HAND MACE - 1 SLOT Your reinforced fist can detach at the end of a yard-long cable or chain, letting you swing it from the end of your arm like a mace. It inflicts 1d6 + Strength Impact damage with a Fighting (Flexible Weapons) attack roll.

SNAKE - 2 SLOTS A flexible cybernetic “snake” lunges out of your body to attack an adjacent foe. It does so as part of your attack action and does not require an Activate action. This counts as a melee attack, generally using Fighting (Brawling). A successful hit does 2d6 Impact damage, but your Strength does not apply. Most often, the snake emerges from your mouth (stored in your throat and upper chest), but it could also emerge from your stomach or another area. A mouth snake can be used as a devastating weapon in an intimate moment, inflicting penetrating damage and allowing you to maintain a grapple or hold on your target while still attacking. For an additional slot, the implant can attack as a minor rather than a major action.

HOLDOUT - 2 SLOTS A gun implanted in your forearm can pop out, firing above the back of your hand, or it can fire through your palm or finger. It does 1d6 + Perception damage with a range of 50 meters. An additional slot can add either 1d6 to the holdout’s damage or double its range to 100 meters.

STUNNER - 2 SLOTS Two of your fingers are modified to act as leads for a powerful electrical discharge when you touch a target with a Fighting (Brawling) roll. A hit inflicts 1d6 Stunning damage, and the target must succeed on a Constitution (Stamina) test with a TN of 10 + the damage inflicted or be paralyzed and unable to take actions for 1d6 rounds. For an additional slot, the stunner fires trailing wires like a stun pistol, making it usable at a range of up to 20 meters.

At the Game Master’s discretion, other weapon implants may be available. Use the Innate Attack enhancement and the existing weapons here as guidelines for creating them.
